<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{bella}Let $(A,\mathfrak{m})$ be a Noetherian local ring and let $I\subseteq \mathfrak{m}$ be an ideal in $A$.  Let $\operatorname{depth} G_I(A) = t$.
 Then $\operatorname{depth} A/I^n \geq t - \ell(I)$ for all $n\geq 1$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
We note that $G_I(A)$ need not have a homogeneous system of parameters. This makes it impossible to prove Theorem \ref{bella} by induction on depth of $G_I(A)$.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor}(with hypotheses as in \ref{bella}). We have 
$$ \operatorname{depth} G_I(A) \leq \ell(I) + \min_{m \geq 1} \{\operatorname{depth} A/I^n \}.$$
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{rachel}
(with setup as in \ref{setup}). We have $\operatorname{projdim}_{\mathcal{S} } L^I = e$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Let $\mathbb{P} $ be a graded, $\mathcal{S} $-projective resolution of $L^I$ of length $e$. Taking the degree $n^{th}$-component of this resolution we get a free resolution (not necessarily minimal) of $A/I^n$ as a $Q$-module.
So $\operatorname{projdim}_Q A/I^n \leq e$ for all $n \geq 1$. From this again by Auslander-Buchsbaum formula we get $\operatorname{depth}_Q A/I^n \geq t - \ell(I)$ for all $n\geq 1$. The result follows as $\operatorname{depth}_A A/I^n =
\operatorname{depth}_Q A/I^n$ (this is an exercise problem in \cite[1.2.26]{BH}).
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
The proof of Theorem \ref{rachel}, although short,  uses the functor $\varprojlim^1$ and so is difficult to guess.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
We first prove that $\operatorname{projdim}_{\mathcal{S} } L \leq e$.
It suffices to prove that if $M$ is a graded $\mathcal{S} $-module then $\operatorname{^*Ext}^{e+1}_\mathcal{S} (L, M) = 0$. As $\{L_r\}_{r\geq 0}$ is an ascending sequence of graded $\mathcal{S} $-submodules of $L$ whose union is $L$, we have an exact sequence for all $v\geq 0$,
\begin{equation*}
  0 \rightarrow \operatorname*{lim^{\rlap{\scriptsize 1}}}_{\longleftarrow} \ \operatorname{^*Ext}^{v-1}_\mathcal{S} (L_r, M) \rightarrow \operatorname{^*Ext}^{v}_\mathcal{S} (L, M) \rightarrow \varprojlim \operatorname{^*Ext}^{v}_\mathcal{S} (L_r, M) \rightarrow 0, \tag{*}
\end{equation*}
 see \cite[3.5.10]{W}.
For $r\ge 1$, by (\ref{Lr-eq}),  we have an exact sequence of $\mathcal{S} $-modules
$$ 0 \rightarrow L_{r-1} \rightarrow L_r \rightarrow G(-r) \rightarrow 0. $$
We apply the functor $\operatorname{^*Hom}(-, M)$ to the above exact sequence and look at the long exact sequence in cohomology. As $\operatorname{projdim}_{\mathcal{S} } G = e$ we obtain surjections
$\operatorname{^*Ext}^e_\mathcal{S} (L_r, M) \rightarrow \operatorname{^*Ext}^e_\mathcal{S} (L_{r-1}, M)$ for all $r\geq 1$ and isomorphisms $\operatorname{^*Ext}^{e+1}_\mathcal{S} (L_r, M) \cong \operatorname{^*Ext}^{e + 1}_\mathcal{S} (L_{r-1}, M)$ for all $r \geq 1$.

The maps $\operatorname{^*Ext}^e_\mathcal{S} (L_r, M) \rightarrow \operatorname{^*Ext}^e_\mathcal{S} (L_{r-1}, M)$ are surjections for $r \geq 1$. So we obtain $\varprojlim^1 \operatorname{^*Ext}^{e}_\mathcal{S} (L_r, M) = 0$, see \cite[3.5.3]{W}.

 For all $r \geq 1$, we have isomorphisms $\operatorname{^*Ext}^{e+1}_\mathcal{S} (L_r, M) \cong \operatorname{^*Ext}^{e + 1}_\mathcal{S} (L_{r-1}, M)$. So  we get for all $r\geq 1$
$$\operatorname{^*Ext}^{e+1}_\mathcal{S} (L_r, M) \cong \operatorname{^*Ext}^{e + 1}_\mathcal{S} (L_{0}, M) = \operatorname{^*Ext}^{e + 1}_\mathcal{S} (G, M) = 0.$$

 The assertion now follows from (*). Thus $\operatorname{projdim}_{\mathcal{S} } L \leq e$.

 Suppose if possible $\operatorname{projdim}_{\mathcal{S} } L <  e$. We have an exact sequence of $\mathcal{S} $-modules
 $$0 \rightarrow G \rightarrow L \rightarrow L(-1) \rightarrow 0, $$
 see \ref{l}.
 Let $k$ be the residue field of $Q$. We apply the functor $-\otimes_{\mathcal{S} } k$  to this exact sequence and consider the long exact  sequence in homology. We obtain $\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal{S} }_e(k, G) = 0$.
 So $\operatorname{projdim}_{\mathcal{S} }G < e$ which is a contradiction. Thus  $\operatorname{projdim}_{\mathcal{S} } L =  e$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
